member.description: Spot misread GT-1 lube oil pressure (floodlight glare)
member.description_longdescription: Gauge reader reported GT-1 lube oil supply pressure as 0.0 bar and threw a low-pressure alert. Actual was 2.4 bar. The new LED floodlight installed above the skid last week completely washes out the gauge in the photo. We went out to check for nothing.

member.description: False thermal alarm GSU T-2 bushing
member.description_longdescription: Got paged at 02:10 for a thermal anomaly on GSU transformer T-2, HV bushing B phase, 92 °C. Control room had T-2 load current at ~1,050 A, well under nameplate, and no top-oil or winding temp alarms in the DCS. Handheld IR on site showed 41 °C. Looks like the robot's thermal reading is off, maybe emissivity setting for the porcelain. Call me on 555-0142 if you want the handheld IR images.

member.description: Thermal hotspot flagged on aux bus duct - suspect reflection
member.description_longdescription: Thermal check flagged a hotspot on the 6.6 kV aux bus duct joint (taken through the IR inspection window). DCS shows bus current was only about 40% of rating at the time, so a real overheating joint is unlikely. Suspect reflection of the room lighting off the window. Thermal alarms should be compared against the actual load before they're raised.

member.description: Evening round cannot finish on one battery
member.description_longdescription: The full evening round (cooling tower -> HRSG -> GT enclosures -> water treatment) can't finish on one battery. Spot heads back to the dock at roughly 78% of waypoints, so the water treatment chemical dosing gauges and the demin tank levels are skipped every single evening. That is 14 measurement points a day we think we have but don't.

member.description: BFP-B low oil alert not seen over weekend
member.description_longdescription: Low oil level alert on BFP-B outboard bearing came in Saturday 22:40 and wasn't seen until Monday morning. Bearing turned out fine and we topped it up, but we lost a day and a half of reaction time on a boiler feed pump.

member.description: Add CEMS shelter to Spot route
member.description_longdescription: Please add the new CEMS shelter to a route. Operators walk there twice a shift to check the sample line heater temperature, the NOx analyzer status lights and the calibration gas bottle pressures. Missing a cal gas bottle running empty can cost us valid emissions data hours. Questions to fatima.haddad@ridgeview-power.example or ext. 4471.

member.description: Spot to read CT basin staff gauge
member.description_longdescription: Nice to have: could Spot read the cooling tower basin staff gauge? We have a level transmitter but it drifts, so a weekly photo to compare would be handy. Not urgent.

member.description: Monthly Spot mission for fire extinguisher checks
member.description_longdescription: Request: a monthly mission that photographs every fire extinguisher pressure gauge and inspection tag on the turbine deck, so we can fill in the fire inspection log from the pictures instead of walking it with a clipboard.

member.description: Spot cannot read GT-1 lube oil sight glass
member.description_longdescription: Oil level check on the GT-1 lube oil reservoir sight glass comes back 'unable to read' about half the time. The glass is stained with varnish and the oil line is hard to see even for a person. Can the model be retrained on dirty glass, or can it flag 'glass needs cleaning' instead of just failing?

Spot's gas payload reported 0 ppm H2S in the condensate polishing area while my personal monitor alarmed at 6 ppm right next to it. If the robot under-reads toxic gas we can't use it as the 'send it in first' check, which was the whole point. When was the gas sensor last bump-tested? Bump-test records should be with Olivia Grant in the lab.
